Thanks for the context — quick engineering read below. High-level: the targets are aggressive but achievable with a combination of continuous batching with strict per-request latency budgets, prefix/KV caching for prompt reuse, and a quantized model variant for the majority of traffic.

Recommended configuration (initial):
- Serving model: redwood-2-base_q8_0 for most routes (q8 quantized; best perf/cost balance). Reserve redwood-2-base_fp16 as a fallthrough for high-quality routes.
- Batching: continuous batching enabled with max_batch_delay = 15ms and max_batch_size tuned to GPU (start with 32). This keeps avg batching latency low while allowing some consolidation for throughput.
- Concurrency: set per-worker concurrency to 8 and scale workers to maintain sustained 60 req/s (we expect ~8 workers on an A100-style pool for 60 req/s depending on prompt size). For spike mitigation, autoscale policy with burst capacity + fast warm pool to cover short 1–5min windows.
- Streaming: use token streaming path (no full-buffering). Ensure first-byte path avoids batching delays by prioritizing the first token in the batch; this is an implementation we support (first-token priority). With the above, first-byte latencies of 40–60ms are achievable in typical cases for q8 models.
- Caching: enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts and session-level cached keys for multi-turn flows. If hit rates are 30%+, cost reduction is substantial (30–35% token reduction on the generation path).
- Quantization/quality: q8_0 preserves most quality for ranking/assistant prompts; recommend an A/B eval on a holdout prompt set (we can run evals) to quantify delta vs fp16.

Cost ballpark: based on their expected mix and using our internal price model:
- redwood-2-base_fp16: ~ $4.50 per 100k generated tokens (example)
- redwood-2-base_q8_0: ~ $2.10 per 100k generated tokens
- redwood-2-small_q8_0 (if acceptable quality): ~ $1.25 per 100k generated tokens
Note: caching and batching effectively reduce billed tokens and GPU time; with 30% cache hit and batching efficiency, we estimate observed unit cost could drop <= 40% vs the baseline above.

Canary plan (48–60h):
- Deploy q8 variant behind a canary flag for 10% of traffic. Collect p50/p95/p99 first-byte and end-to-end latencies, token/sec throughput, cache hit rate, and quality regression metrics on a prompt holdout.
- Rollback to fp16 fallback if quality drop > 2% on key metrics or p95 increases beyond 10% of target.

I'll prepare a short perf-estimate CSV (redwood-perf-estimate.csv) with expected latency profiles and worker counts for their given traffic numbers and attach. Happy to join the Wed 10:00 PT call to walk through this and the workbook.
